**What you should be able to do after this meeting.** Draw the graph for an experiment, an instrument, and a discontinuity, and say whether any of the three could work for your question.

The opening quiz is on this reading.

## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Three designs, each drawn before it is described. Experiments: randomisation cuts every arrow into treatment, so there is no back door left to close. Instrumental variables: an arrow into treatment and none into the outcome except through it — the exclusion restriction is that missing arrow, which is why it cannot be tested. Regression discontinuity: nothing else jumps at the cutoff. For each: what variation it exploits, what it assumes, how it fails, and what it looks like done well

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

Each team draws a setting nobody in the room owns — a bank with an email list, a scholarship cutoff, an NGO that gave filters to whoever asked. Fifteen minutes to draw the graph, name a design, and state the assumption carrying it. Then you defend it at the front for four minutes while the room attacks: what breaks this? One card cannot be answered honestly at all, and the team holding it has to be willing to say so. Last: is an experiment, an instrument, or a discontinuity actually open to your own project? Most teams find the answer is no, and finding that out today rather than in November is the point

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.
